findings.description: The new prose claims the one mechanism "disables every customisation the machine brings" and "disables all of them at once", and line 68 concludes "What covers later is the customisations not loading at all". The vendor documents `--safe-mode` (the mechanism, per internal/agent/claude.go:24) as leaving the managed settings policy in force, explicitly including policy-configured hooks, status line and file-suggestion commands; only managed plugins, managed skills, managed CLAUDE.md and policy-configured MCP servers stop loading. A hook is exactly the source the paragraph above (line 48) names as one the vendor's tool restriction never covered, and a hook contributes no entry to the session's tool list, so the opening-event check at internal/agent/claude.go:91-104 cannot see it either. Concrete path: on the very kind of machine the change measured on (design.md:30, a deployed managed configuration), a policy-configured hook runs in the reviewer's session, writes outside the snapshot worktree where nothing socrates holds bounds it, and every mechanism this requirement names reads clean. The change's measurement (design.md:32-36) covered external sources and one plugin tool, not policy hooks. The same sentence is in openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:36 and both scenarios (openspec/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:83, delta:63), and the same overstatement is now carried by the invariant at AGENTS.md:98. Either the coverage claim needs the managed-policy carve-out stated, or a person needs to decide that the residual is accepted and say so.

The requirement this change rewrote still says "It SHALL load user-level settings and memory only", two paragraphs above the new sentence requiring the machine's customisations to be disabled. The vendor documents that mechanism as disabling CLAUDE.md and auto memory, and the change's own design.md:42 states it "takes the user's own memory and skills out of the reviewer". So the promoted requirement now demands memory the change deliberately removes: an implementer reading it would add back a memory source, and a reviewer checking conformance cannot tell which of the two sentences wins. The invariant at AGENTS.md:97 has the accurate form ("The reviewer loads user settings only") — the specification's "and memory" is the stale half. Same sentence at openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:24.

The new prose names one honest limit of the tool list (a source that connects after the opening event) but not the one that is silent: an opening event carrying no `tools` field at all. internal/agent/stream.go:93 assigns whatever the init event held, and internal/agent/claude.go:110-120 returns no unexpected tools for an empty list, so a vendor release that stops emitting `tools` turns "the mechanism SHALL NOT be trusted to have worked" (line 62) into a check that passes on absence of evidence, with no event recorded and nothing for a person to look at. The unit tests guard against this with an explicit "would pass on an empty reading" fatal (internal/agent/claude_test.go:80-82, 328-329), which is exactly the case production code does not distinguish; the weekly fidelity guard pins the field's presence against recordings rather than failing a live run.

The new scenario and the rewritten prose were applied to the promoted specification at the same time as to the change's delta, while the change is still under way (tasks.md:58 is open). The drop gate reads the promoted spec as the before-state (internal/promotion/promotion.go:134,168), so with both sides identical `ScenariosDropped` cannot fire for this change: the pre-`make scenario-drop` run recorded in tasks.md:56 exercises nothing, and the five scenario renames declared at openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:3-16 — the reason the gate was taught renames in the preceding commit — now match no promoted name, including a FROM/TO pair that is identical on both sides (delta:6-7). The archive skill treats an already-synced state as legitimate, so this costs nothing at archive time; it does mean the gate provides no evidence about this change.

risk_rationale: The change is prose-only and the code it describes already exists and is tested on the delivered invocation, but the rewritten requirement overstates what the one mechanism covers and leaves a contradicting sentence about memory in the same requirement, both of which mislead about a security property.
